## Open

### F-334 — A passing Storybook run rewrites 22 committed markup snapshots

> _2026-10-01 · tools/blong-log · open_

Running `npm run storybook:test:ci` in tools/blong-log leaves the working tree dirty: the runner
writes src/client/__markup_snapshots__/*.json on every run from .storybook/test-runner.cjs, which is
an analysis artifact and not a jest comparison, so what it writes depends on the browser it ran
with. Chromium 1243 serializes a computed style as `overflow: clip` where the committed file says
`visible`, so one run produced 22 modified files that a commit would have to explain and that no
assertion depends on. The 21 image snapshots in __image_snapshots__ are the comparison that matters;
those passed. Worth either listing the markup snapshots in .gitignore or normalising the style
properties they carry, so a local run does not hand the author a diff they did not ask for.

### F-531 — The CI storybook leg served a dev server whose output went into the log

> _2026-10-15 · tools/blong-log · open_

`tools/blong-log` was the only package whose `ci-test` ran a Storybook dev server: the chain
`blong-dev test || …; node --run storybook:test:ci` started `storybook dev`, so the CI log carried
the server's banner and its Vite build chatter next to the test results — the "not aligned with the
rest" the package's own skill already describes the other way round ("build static → serve → test →
exit"). `core/blong-browser` has the same script but never calls it from `ci-test`, which is why it
never showed.

The script now runs `storybook dev --ci --quiet --loglevel warn` with its output redirected to a
temp file, and prints that file only when the test runner fails — the log carries the tests'
results, and the server's output is still there for the failure that needs it. Verified by running
the script: 22 story tests pass and no banner or Vite line reaches the log.
